realRailsNow: TN12 covenant proofs for vault, assurance, and escrow

categories.name: DEX / AMM
categories.targetUseCase: Users swap assets or provide liquidity to pools.
categories.repoPosition: Do not build a live DEX claim yet. Build pool/risk briefs and, later, accepted intent or settlement drafts.

questions.question: How are pool reserves represented?
questions.currentAnswer: No live shared pool state exists in this repo. Current work can represent intents or registry state through accepted payloads, but not a covenant-enforced AMM reserve pair.
questions.existingRail: accepted transaction payloads and indexer-derived app state
questions.missingRail: shared pool state or rollup/vProg execution state
questions.nextArtifact: Pool reserve brief with a fake-state simulator, not custody.

questions.question: Who can update reserves?
questions.currentAnswer: No reserve update authority is implemented. A future design must decide whether updates are covenant spends, wallet-reviewed settlement transactions, rollup state transitions, or app-indexer records.
questions.missingRail: reserve update authority and enforcement model
questions.nextArtifact: Authority matrix: user swap, LP add/remove, admin pause, and invalid update cases.

questions.question: How is swap price calculated?
questions.currentAnswer: Only research references exist. No constant-product, concentrated-liquidity, or order-book pricing engine is implemented for Kaspa settlement.
questions.missingRail: pricing engine tied to enforceable reserves
questions.nextArtifact: Simulation-only constant-product calculator with price-impact warnings.

questions.question: How is slippage enforced?
questions.currentAnswer: Not implemented. Slippage can be displayed in a simulator, but enforcement needs a transaction or state transition that fails when output is below minimum.
questions.existingRail: local signed drafts and wallet review
questions.missingRail: min-output enforcement in covenant, wallet, rollup, or vProg path
questions.nextArtifact: Draft-level min-output review field before any settlement claim.

questions.question: How are LP shares tracked?
questions.currentAnswer: Not implemented. LP accounting needs native assets, issuer-indexed shares, or a future shared-state execution surface.
questions.existingRail: simple asset policy and issuer-indexer patterns
questions.missingRail: LP share asset/accounting model
questions.nextArtifact: LP-share accounting brief comparing issuer-indexed shares versus future native/covenant shares.

questions.question: How is ordering or MEV handled?
questions.currentAnswer: Current auction/intent work names MEV caveats but does not solve ordering. Fast accepted payloads are not MEV protection.
questions.existingRail: accepted payload state and auction intent registry
questions.missingRail: ordering policy, batch auction, or sequencing commitment design
questions.nextArtifact: MEV/order caveat checklist for all swap and auction prototypes.

categories.smallestHonestPrototype: AMM risk and UX simulator plus accepted swap-intent payload registry with no custody or live swap claim.

categories.name: Lending / Borrowing
categories.targetUseCase: Users deposit collateral, borrow against it, repay, or get liquidated when health falls below threshold.
categories.repoPosition: Build risk dashboards and accepted receipt accounting first. Do not claim a lending market.

questions.question: Where does collateral sit?
questions.currentAnswer: No lending collateral vault exists. Escrow/vault proofs show covenant custody patterns, but not multi-borrower collateral accounting.
questions.existingRail: TN12 vault and escrow covenant proofs
questions.missingRail: collateral custody model for lending positions
questions.nextArtifact: Collateral position schema that marks custody as simulated, wallet-policy, covenant, or future vProg.

questions.question: Who can liquidate?
questions.currentAnswer: No liquidation role or transaction path exists. Any design must specify permissionless liquidators, keeper set, issuer/admin action, or manual review.
questions.missingRail: liquidation transaction path and authority model
questions.nextArtifact: Liquidation role matrix with stale-price and bad-liquidation cases.

questions.question: What oracle gives the price?
questions.currentAnswer: The repo has attestation research and stable-value comparisons, not a production price oracle.
questions.existingRail: attestation registry and accepted signal payloads
questions.missingRail: price oracle trust model and dispute process
questions.nextArtifact: Oracle-source checklist: issuer, reporter set, external feed, challenge window, stale-price rule.

questions.question: What happens if the oracle is wrong or stale?
questions.currentAnswer: No automatic protection exists. Current docs require explicit oracle/source assumptions before product claims.
questions.missingRail: stale-price guard, pause rule, dispute path, and bad-liquidation rollback policy
questions.nextArtifact: Stale-oracle failure-mode simulator.

questions.question: How are interest and health factors tracked?
questions.currentAnswer: Not implemented. A non-custodial dashboard could calculate health from accepted receipts and manual prices before settlement.
questions.existingRail: accepted transaction receipts and indexer replay rows
questions.missingRail: position accounting and interest-rate model
questions.nextArtifact: Simulation-only health factor calculator.

categories.smallestHonestPrototype: Manual risk dashboard fed by accepted deposit/repay receipts and explicit external prices, with no borrowing custody.

categories.name: Perps / Prediction / Hedge Markets
categories.targetUseCase: Users express event or price exposure, margin positions, or review hedge risk.
categories.repoPosition: The simulator may suggest review prompts from accepted attestations, but it must not trade, custody, settle, price real markets, or give advice.

questions.question: What oracle decides settlement?
questions.currentAnswer: No settlement oracle exists. Current markets use accepted attestation or public observation as simulation inputs only.
questions.missingRail: settlement oracle, dispute window, and final resolution rule
questions.nextArtifact: Resolution-source matrix per market.

questions.question: Where is margin or collateral held?
questions.currentAnswer: Nowhere. Current positions are manual simulator entries with notional TKAS values, not locked funds.
questions.missingRail: margin custody and withdrawal/liquidation rules
questions.nextArtifact: No-funds position accounting model before custody.

questions.question: How are positions matched?
questions.currentAnswer: Not implemented. There is no order book, AMM, counterparty matcher, or clearing engine.
questions.missingRail: matching engine or market-making model
questions.nextArtifact: Paper-position matching simulator.

questions.question: Who can close or liquidate?
questions.currentAnswer: No close/liquidate authority exists. Current output is only review suggested/watch state.
questions.missingRail: close, liquidation, and dispute authority
questions.nextArtifact: Authority and failure-mode brief.

questions.question: What prevents fake odds or stale prices?
questions.currentAnswer: Only source signature review exists. Reputation thresholds still need hardening, and draft signals cannot move market probability.
questions.missingRail: reputation thresholds, stale signal rules, market manipulation controls
questions.nextArtifact: Attestation reputation threshold artifact.

categories.smallestHonestPrototype: Simulation-only board with accepted signal history, stale-signal review, and no trading, custody, or advice.

categories.name: Bridge / Source-Chain Apps
categories.targetUseCase: Users prove events or asset state from another chain and use Kaspa for receipts, settlement, or claims.
categories.repoPosition: Do not claim trustless bridging. ZK proves a statement about selected inputs; it does not by itself prove source-chain canonicality.

questions.question: What is the canonical source-chain anchor?
questions.currentAnswer: Not selected. Possible anchors include a light client, finality certificate, accumulated-work view, reporter set, or challenge process.
questions.missingRail: canonical source-chain anchor
questions.nextArtifact: Anchor-choice matrix.

questions.question: Who verifies source-chain finality?
questions.currentAnswer: No verifier is implemented. A future bridge must state whether finality is verified by script, ZK proof, reporter quorum, or manual review.
questions.missingRail: finality verifier and trust model
questions.nextArtifact: Finality trust-model checklist.

questions.question: Where do bridged assets sit?
questions.currentAnswer: No wrapped asset or custody bridge exists. External stablecoin rail remains integration research.
questions.missingRail: custody, mint/burn, exit, and redemption policy
questions.nextArtifact: Bridge custody and exit brief.

questions.question: What happens during reorg, fraud, or challenge?
questions.currentAnswer: No challenge process exists. The indexer has rollback guards for Kaspa accepted-state reads, not cross-chain fraud proofs.
questions.missingRail: cross-chain challenge and fraud handling
questions.nextArtifact: Challenge-period state machine.

categories.smallestHonestPrototype: Receipt mapper and anchor checklist that records source-chain proof assumptions without minting wrapped assets.

categories.name: Stable-Value / Redeemable Units
categories.targetUseCase: Users hold or redeem a less volatile unit while using Kaspa payment and receipt rails.
categories.repoPosition: Issuer-backed redemption state can be modeled now. Native or overcollateralized stablecoins remain research.

questions.question: Who backs redemption?
questions.currentAnswer: For the buildable path, a known issuer backs redemption. Other paths need collateral, oracle, or external-chain assumptions.
questions.missingRail: reserve attestation and legal redemption process
questions.nextArtifact: Issuer reserve and redemption policy fixture.

questions.question: Where is collateral?
questions.currentAnswer: No collateral vault exists for a stable unit. Overcollateralized and synthetic designs are research only.
questions.existingRail: vault covenant proofs as primitive examples
questions.missingRail: collateral vault, mint/burn, and liquidation rules
questions.nextArtifact: Collateral health simulator with manual prices.

questions.question: What oracle or reserve report is trusted?
questions.currentAnswer: No production reserve oracle exists. Accepted payloads can record issuer actions but cannot prove reserves by themselves.
questions.missingRail: reserve report source and audit model
questions.nextArtifact: Reserve disclosure and stale-report review rules.

categories.smallestHonestPrototype: Issuer redemption ledger with accepted issuance/redemption payloads and explicit reserve-trust label.
